sourcedFrom: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 (01/2008 (printed as the document code G0037602 - 01/2008 on the last page, PDF p.118; no separate copyright line))
cleanIntro: The Super Black Eagle II is INERTIA-driven, not gas-driven. There is no gas piston, no gas ports and no gas cylinder to clean — the action is a spring between the bolt body and the rotating locking head. So the parts that matter are the bolt assembly, the firing mechanism in the trigger guard, and the bore. Benelli's position is that the gun needs no special maintenance; what it needs is that the bolt and the trigger group do not stay clogged with powder residue. Printed page numbers are cited; the book is printed in several languages side by side, and only its English text is quoted.

steps.title: Safety catch on — the red ring must disappear
steps.action: Press the safety button in the trigger guard until the RED RING is no longer visible. Red showing means the gun will fire; the check is visual and takes a second.
steps.prose: Benelli defines the safe state by what you cannot see rather than by which way the button points, which is the more reliable test on a gun built in both right- and left-hand versions.
steps.quote: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until its red ring, indicating firing position, is no longer visible (figs. 16-17).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Safety catch — printed p.28

steps.title: Open the bolt and eject the chambered shell
steps.action: With the safety engaged and the muzzle in a safe direction, rest the stock on your hip and pull the cocking lever back. The chambered shell is extracted and thrown clear. Then ease the cocking lever forward with your hand to close the breech — do not let it slam.
steps.quote: 1) Engage the safety catch; rest the stock on your hip and pull the cocking lever to open the bolt (fig. 22): the cartridge in the chamber is extracted and ejected from the gun. 2) Gently release the cocking lever to close the breech block (fig. 15).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Unloading — printed p.42

steps.title: Empty the magazine one shell at a time
steps.action: Turn the gun over, push the carrier down, and press the front of the cartridge retaining lever sideways with your index finger. One shell drops into your hand per press — press again for each shell until the tube is empty.
steps.prose: The lever holds the column, so one press releases exactly one shell. Do not expect them to cascade, and do not stop counting until the tube is truly empty.
steps.quote: 3) Reverse the gun, and, thrusting the carrier down, press sideways the cartridge retaining lever from the front with the hand index finger (fig. 23). 4) The cartridges will be released one by one into your hand (fig. 24); the carrier latch must be pressed for each released cartridge.
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Unloading — printed p.44

steps.title: Prove chamber and magazine empty
steps.action: Before a single part comes off, look into the chamber and the magazine and confirm both are empty. Benelli puts this instruction at the head of the stripping procedure and of every other operation in the book.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber and the magazine are unloaded! (Carefully read the instructions on gun loading and unloading).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance) — printed p.56
steps.warn: Check the carrier too. A shell resting on the carrier is not in the chamber and not in the tube, and it is the one that gets missed.

steps.title: Lock the bolt open
steps.action: Draw the bolt lever back until the bolt locks open. If it will not stay open, move the cartridge drop lever the way the manual's arrow shows and try again.
steps.quote: 1) Open the bolt by pulling back the bolt lever (fig. 18) until the bolt is locked open. Should the bolt fail to engage, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat the operation (fig. 6).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.56

steps.title: Pull the bolt handle out
steps.action: Pull the bolt handle straight out of the bolt with one firm tug. It is a friction fit, so one decisive pull works better than several gentle ones.
steps.quote: 2) Pull the bolt handle off with a firm tug (fig. 26).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.58

steps.title: Fore-end cap off the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap from the front of the magazine tube and take it right off. Put it where it cannot roll away — it is the one fastener that holds the front of the gun together.
steps.quote: 3) Unscrew the fore-end cap and remove from magazine tube (fig. 27).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.58

steps.title: Barrel, cover and fore-end forward off the tube
steps.action: Rest the stock against your hip. Hold the stock-and-receiver unit in one hand and the barrel-cover-fore-end unit in the other, and pull the front unit FORWARD until it comes completely off the magazine tube.
steps.prose: The barrel is not screwed or pinned on this gun. It slides on the magazine tube and is held to the receiver by the fore-end cap, which is why the whole front comes off as one piece.
steps.quote: 4) While resting the stock against your hip, grab the stock-receiver unit with a hand and the barrel-cover-fore-end unit with the other hand (fig. 28). Pull the latter forward and completely off the tube magazine (fig. 29).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.58

steps.title: Separate the fore-end from the barrel
steps.action: Rotate the barrel-cover-fore-end unit the way the manual's arrow shows, then draw the fore-end off the barrel guide ring.
steps.quote: 5) Rotate the barrel-cover-fore-end unit in the direction shown by the arrow (fig. 30) and separate it from the barrel by pulling it out of the barrel guide ring (fig. 31).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.60

steps.title: Ease the bolt forward against the recoil spring
steps.action: Hold the bolt assembly with one hand so you are pushing back against the recoil spring, press the carrier release button, and let the bolt come forward slowly until the spring stops pushing it. Do NOT let it fly.
steps.prose: The recoil spring is pushing on the bolt, and the carrier release button is what lets it go. Your hand on the bolt is the only thing controlling it.
steps.quote: 6) While holding the bolt assembly with a hand (fig. 5) so as to counter-balance the thrust of the recoil spring, push the carrier release button (fig. 15) and ease the bolt forward until the recoil spring no longer pushes it forward (fig. 32).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.60
steps.warn: The recoil spring is compressed behind the bolt. Keep a hand on the bolt through this whole step.

steps.title: Bolt assembly out along its guides
steps.action: Draw the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along the guides it runs on rather than lifting it out.
steps.quote: 7) Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides (fig. 33).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.60

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin, firing pin and spring
steps.action: Hold the firing pin and its spring in place with a thumb — they are under spring pressure — then take out the firing pin retaining pin. Only once the retaining pin is clear do you let go and remove the firing pin and its spring.
steps.prose: Hold first, pull the pin second. That order stops the firing pin shooting out of the bolt when the retaining pin comes out.
steps.quote: 8) Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly, while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place (fig. 34). 9) Remove the firing pin and firing pin spring from the bolt (fig. 35).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.62

steps.title: Locking head off the bolt — field strip complete
steps.action: Take the locking head pin out of the bolt, then slide the locking head off the bolt. That completes the field strip: bolt handle, fore-end cap, fore-end, barrel, bolt assembly, firing pin group and locking head.
steps.prose: The rotating locking head is the working end of the inertia system, and its stem and lugs are what you are about to clean. Benelli's procedure goes on to the inertia spring and the trigger guard assembly; that is the DEEP CLEAN branch.
steps.quote: 10) Remove the locking head pin from the bolt (fig. 36). 11) Remove the bolt locking head from the bolt (fig. 37).
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.62

steps.title: Bore after every outing
steps.action: Clean the barrel after every use. The bore is chromium plated inside, so you are removing fouling rather than fighting rust in the bore.
steps.quote: 1) normal cleaning of the barrel after use;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Maintenance — printed p.52

steps.title: Internal choke out, threads clean
steps.action: Unscrew the internal choke with the toothed choke wrench supplied with the gun and draw it right out of the barrel. If the threaded seat in the muzzle is dirty, clean it before the choke goes back in.
steps.prose: A choke left in place through season after season can seize in its threads. Benelli recommends cleaning the choke and its thread before the gun is put away.
steps.quote: 1) Unscrew the internal choke using the special choke wrench supplied with the shotgun and extract it completely from the barrel seat (fig. 59). 2) If the threaded seat of the choke on the barrel is too dirty, clean it.
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Internal choke — printed p.100
steps.warn: NOTE: before re-using the shotgun, make sure that the choke wrench has been removed from the barrel’s muzzle.

steps.title: Bolt assembly — dismantled, cleaned, lubricated
steps.action: The bolt collects the same residue as the trigger group, and Benelli asks for it to be taken apart, cleaned and lubricated regularly — which is the strip you have just done. Clean the locking head's lugs and stem, the firing pin channel and the firing pin itself.
steps.prose: On an inertia gun a gummy locking-head stem is a common cause of failure to cycle, because the spring between head and body has to move freely for the action to work at all.
steps.quote: 3) the bolt assembly may also become clogged with the same material and must be periodically dismantled, cleaned and lubricated;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Maintenance — printed p.52

steps.title: Firing mechanism — clean out the powder residue
steps.action: The hammer, trigger and the rest of the firing mechanism clog with powder residue and dirt. Clean and lubricate them periodically. Benelli's own troubleshooting list names a dirty firing mechanism as a reason the gun fails to fire.
steps.quote: 2) the firing mechanism, consisting of ham- mer, trigger, etc., may become clogged with any powder residuals (or foreign matters). Remove this by periodical cleaning or lubrication;
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Maintenance — printed p.52

steps.title: Oil what corrodes
steps.action: Oil the parts exposed to the weather — receiver, bolt and barrel exterior. Benelli specifies its own cleaning set and oil.
steps.quote: 4) to keep the gun in good order, oiling of the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion is recommended.
steps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Maintenance — printed p.54

deepSteps.title: Inertia spring out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: With the locking head off, take the inertia spring out of its seat in the bolt body. This is the spring the whole action depends on, so clean it and its seat and check it moves freely.
deepSteps.prose: On reassembly this spring MUST go back between the locking head and the bolt body. Benelli warns that leaving it out risks a shot being fired as the bolt closes.
deepSteps.quote: 12) Remove the inertia spring from its seat in the bolt (fig. 38).
deepSteps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.64
deepSteps.warn: NOTE: always make sure that the bolt recoil spring is positioned between the locking head and the bolt itself, in order to avoid a shot being fired when the bolt is closed.

deepSteps.title: Trigger group stop plug out
deepSteps.action: Push the trigger group stop plug out of the stock-and-receiver unit from either side, using the tip of the firing pin you have just removed or a punch.
deepSteps.quote: 13) Extract the trigger group stop plug from the stock-receiver unit, thrusting it from right or left with the point of the same firing pin or punch (fig. 39).
deepSteps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.64
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: when the pistol grip stock is installed on the shotgun the stock must be loosened before the trigger guard assembly can be removed from the receiver.

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard assembly out to the front — fully stripped
deepSteps.action: Press the carrier release button and slide the trigger guard assembly out of the receiver towards the FRONT. If your gun has a pistol grip stock, partly unscrew the stock retaining nut first so the stock moves back enough to free the group. That is Benelli's complete strip; the book takes the gun no further.
deepSteps.prose: Benelli's procedure stops here, with every part that needs routine cleaning already separated. Do not take the trigger guard assembly itself apart.
deepSteps.aside: The shotgun is now completely stripped. All the parts that require routine maintenance and cleaning are disassembled.
deepSteps.quote: 14) Press the carrier release button and extract the trigger guard assembly towards the front (fig. 40).
deepSteps.cite: SUPER BLACK EAGLE II — Use • Maintenance — G0037602 - 01/2008 — Stripping procedure — printed p.64

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Clean the bore after every use.
The bore is chromium plated inside — clean the fouling out, do not scour it.
Internal choke out with the choke wrench; clean the choke and the threaded seat in the muzzle.
⚠ Take the choke wrench out of the muzzle before the gun is used again.

cleaning.name: Bolt assembly
tasks: Locking head: clean both lugs, the stem and the locking head pin.
Firing pin and firing pin spring: clean them and the channel through the bolt body.
Inertia spring and its seat (Deep Clean): clean, and check the spring moves freely.

cleaning.name: Firing mechanism
tasks: Hammer, trigger and the rest of the group: clean off powder residue and dirt.
Lubricate lightly. A clogged firing mechanism is a listed cause of a failure to fire.

cleaning.name: Receiver and exterior
tasks: Oil the parts exposed to the weather.
Wipe the receiver, magazine tube and barrel exterior.

reassembly: Deep Clean only: trigger guard assembly back in with the hammer COCKED — press the carrier button, set the front of the group against the receiver, then push it fully home. Push the trigger guard pin through from either side until it is fully in. On a pistol grip stock, retighten the stock retaining nut fully.
Deep Clean only: inertia spring back into its seat in the bolt. It MUST sit between the locking head and the bolt body.
Locking head into the bolt with the hole in its stem lined up with the slot in the bolt. The slanted surfaces on the stem should NOT be visible when it is in correctly.
Locking head pin through the slot into the stem. The reference line on top of the pin must be visible and lined up with the bolt's centerline.
Firing pin and firing pin spring into the bolt — always together — then the firing pin retaining pin into its seat so it holds the firing pin.
Hold the stock-and-receiver almost vertical and slide the bolt assembly onto its guides. The link must slide over the trigger guard assembly and onto the recoil spring plunger inside the receiver.
Lock the bolt open. Fore-end onto the barrel: slide it over the barrel guide ring, then snap it onto the barrel.

Barrel-cover-fore-end unit onto the magazine tube with the cover over the tube and centred on the receiver, and push it all the way home until it clicks against metal and the cover sits flush on the receiver.
Fore-end cap screwed all the way on and tightened firmly so the barrel unit is held tight against the receiver.
Bolt handle pushed fully into the bolt, then close the bolt by pressing the carrier button.
fncheck: With the gun proven empty and the muzzle in a safe direction: pull the bolt lever back and confirm the bolt locks open, then press the carrier button and confirm it runs forward and closes fully. Cycle it by hand several times. Engage the safety and confirm the red ring on the button disappears; release it and confirm the red ring shows. Confirm the fore-end cap is tight and the choke wrench is not in the muzzle. If the gun fails to fire in use, Benelli's troubleshooting list includes checking the firing mechanism and cleaning and lubricating it if necessary.
